Header:
Date: 2026-03-18

Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jared Mills (LifeCare CTO), Tanya Rivera (Product Ops), Samir Patel (SRE), Lena Ortiz (PM)

SUMMARY (auto): Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limits, quotas and org/project keys. Covered UI and API examples, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and security controls.

---
Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Alex with Redwood, i've got Priya the SE with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jared Mills: Doing well, thanks. busy week but looking forward to this. Tanya set this up cause we're trying to lock down multi-tenant controls for our new patient messaging feature.
[00:15] Tanya Rivera: yea we need per-team billing and also tight quotas per customer org.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Great, we'll walk through org keys and project keys and show how you can apply rate limits and quotas at both levels. we'll demo console and then the API examples.
[00:29] Lena Ortiz: high level first pls, whats difference between org and project keys?
[00:32] Priya Nair: Sure. Org key is the top-level identifier that maps to your LifeCare account. Projects are children under orgs, e.g. prod, staging, tenant-a. you can attach quota policies at org or project level. default behavior is inheritance - project picks up org limits unless you override.
[00:46] Samir Patel: ok and billing is at org level right? we want to bill customers per project though, possible?
[00:50] Alex Chen: Yes billing is flexible — by default invoices are org-level, but you can map project usage to external billing centers; we give usage breakout per project so you can export CSVs and ingest into your billing system.
[01:02] Priya Nair: I'll show the console now.
[01:05] [Screen share starts - Console - Rate Limits page]
[01:12] Priya Nair: on the left you can see "Policies". here's a policy we've named "tenant-default" that sets a token bucket of 100 qps with a burst of 200 and daily token quota 8M tokens. you can attach that policy to an org or to an individual project.
[01:29] Jared Mills: the term tokens, is that tokens in the model sense or request tokens? we need to map to our internal terminology.
[01:34] Priya Nair: it's per-token from a billing vantage for text gen; for rate limiting the UI exposes both requests-per-second (rps) and tokens-per-second. so you can limit by either. apologies the export sometimes labels it as "token-rate" which is confusing — transcription note: UI label is token-rate.
[01:49] Tanya Rivera: if a project exceeds its daily token quota does it fail or degrade? we don't want to drop messages silently.
[01:55] Alex Chen: great question. you can choose behavior: hard reject (429) or soft degrade where we route to a cheaper model variant or to a cached response. for miss we also emit webhooks and logs to your org audit stream.
[02:07] Samir Patel: how immediate is the quota enforcement? we have spikes, you mentioned bursts. can we do a sliding window?
[02:12] Priya Nair: It's token-bucket based, so bursts are allowed up to the configured burst. enforcement is near-real-time; avg lat to react is under a second. we also provide per-key metrics so you can build autoscaling triggers. caveat: very small buckets + huge fanout can cause small windows, but we have mitigations.
[02:28] Jared Mills: curious about multi-tenant isolation. if tenant A hits crazy usage does it affect other projects on the same org or pool?
[02:33] Alex Chen: by default projects are logically isolated for rate limits; on shared hosted capacity we do fair-share routing and optional reservation. if you need strict isolation we recommend Dedicated where you reserve GPU pools per-customer.
[02:44] Lena Ortiz: what's the overhead to add Dedicated for a single customer? procurement wise.
[02:48] Alex Chen: That goes into committed capacity model — minimum commitments apply and we can share a template in the pricing pack. for pilot you can also run a private project in host with stronger per-key caps to emulate isolation.
[03:00] Priya Nair: back to the console — you can also attach rate limits at the API key level. so you create project keys scoped to a project and give them different quotas.
[03:10] Tanya Rivera: we have SSO and want role-based controls so ops can create project keys but devs can't change billing. does Redwood integrate with our SAML provider?
[03:18] Priya Nair: Yes SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning. you can map groups to RBAC roles and restrict who can create org-level policies. example: only admins can change org quotas, team leads can create project keys.
[03:30] Samir Patel: does the audit log show who changed what and when? We need that for compliance.
[03:33] Alex Chen: Yep, full audit trail, plus exportable logs to your SIEM. We also support customer-managed KMS so key wraps are under your control.
[03:43] Jared Mills: Good. i want to understand throttling behavior end-to-end; like what does the client see at 429 and what do we get in the headers?
[03:50] Priya Nair: We return standard 429 with Retry-After. In the response headers we add X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and a x-redwood-project-id so you can correlate. Also a header with the policy id.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: could you show a curl example?
[04:07] Priya Nair: sure. [types] curl -H "Authorization: Bearer PROJECT_KEY" https... and you'll get the headers i mentioned. Also we have an SDK helper that will automatically backoff according to Retry-After. note: the current sample in docs has an old header name 'x-rw-limit' — we'll update that.
[04:24] Jared Mills: are there ways to whitelist certain internal IPs or services from rate limits?
[04:28] Alex Chen: yes, you can create exception rules by source identity or by tag; for instance mark internal worker keys as "system" which bypasses the token-bucket and uses a higher quota. but we recommend cautious use.
[04:40] Samir Patel: For HIPAA we need data residency and audit. does rate-limit logging capture full request metadata? what's redaction policy?
[04:48] Priya Nair: Logs capture request metadata (timestamp, project id, model id, token usage) and a truncated prompt hash — we do not log PHI by default. For HIPAA deployments we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS and disable transcript logging. We'll include the security pack with specifics.
[05:05] Tanya Rivera: We're leaning towards mixed model: hosted for low-volume tenants and dedicated reserved pools for our largest partners. does that mix complicate rate-limiting config?
[05:12] Alex Chen: Not really — the control plane is unified. Policies are universal and you can express routing rules: e.g. if project has tag "premium" route to dedicated pool and apply a different quota. If dedicated is down we'll fallback to a compatible hosted variant if you allow fallback.
[05:28] Lena Ortiz: What about cost controls? we want automatic throttles when spend crosses thresholds.
[05:33] Priya Nair: You can set monetary caps tied to org or billing center. when threshold hits we can either limit token rates or block generation. We also have alerting hooks so finance gets notified.
[05:44] Jared Mills: demoing the API console again; can we see the project usage page?
[05:48] [Screen shows Project Usage dashboard]
[05:55] Priya Nair: Here's the breakdown by project and API key. notice you can also click into a time window and export the raw events. those events include approximate token counts and latency percentiles.
[06:11] Jared Mills: latency percentiles — is tail latency impacted by rate limiting? curious about p95/p99.
[06:15] Priya Nair: Rate limiting itself is a gate, not adding latency. But under high queueing you might see some queuing delay; we show p50/p95/p99 in the dashboard and we also compute token-cost per route.
[06:27] Samir Patel: For the pilot, we want to try a scenario: peak of ~800 rps for 5 mins for a single tenant. will the hosted pool handle it?
[06:34] Alex Chen: Depends on model and token lengths. We can run a short benchmark. If you need guaranteed headroom, Dedicated with reserved capacity is the path. For pilot we can provision burst capacity on Hosted and monitor.
[06:46] Tanya Rivera: ok what's the typical turnaround to spin up a dedicated pool?
[06:50] Alex Chen: For standard sizes it's a few days after contract; for pilot we can do a temporary reserved allocation in 24-48 hours depending on region. we'll confirm in the pricing pack.
[06:59] Lena Ortiz: about per-customer keys: can we rotate keys and revoke without impacting other projects?
[07:03] Priya Nair: yes keys are scoped and revocation is atomic for that key. rotating keys is supported via the console or API, and you can create new keys with overlapping valid windows.
[07:15] Jared Mills: Any gotchas with SDKs? will our serverless functions get 429s unexpectedly?
[07:20] Priya Nair: If you hit sudden cold-start storms, you'll see 429s. we recommend token caching at your service edge and client-side retry with exponential backoff. the SDK has built-in retry strategies tuned for redwood.
[07:33] Samir Patel: I saw mention earlier of routing policies. can we route based on region for data residency?
[07:38] Alex Chen: yes region-aware routing exists. you can set policies to prefer a region and failover to another in emergencies. for strict residency we do Private deployments where compute is in your VPC.
[07:48] Tanya Rivera: ok, last set of questions then a recap. when a project uses up its daily tokens does it zero out at midnight org timezone? can we align to customer timezone?
[07:57] Priya Nair: Default is UTC rollovers but you can set org-level timezone for quota reset; per-project timezone overrides also supported.
[08:06] Lena Ortiz: we'll need the docs for the exact header names and sample curl, and the security pack.
[08:10] Alex Chen: we'll send those. Priya, any final notes?
[08:13] Priya Nair: two more things — we support per-route quotas (so you can limit chat endpoints separately from embeddings) and a feature called "cost caps" that stops generation when projected spend exceeds a threshold in the billing period. we'll include sample configs. also note small transcription typo earlier: KV cache was spelled as KV cash in a previous doc.
[08:31] Jared Mills: Great. Next steps for us is to confirm pilot scope and HIPAA items. thanks this was helpful.
[08:36] Alex Chen: Thanks all. we'll follow up with pricing + security pack and propose pilot start dates.
[08:40] Tanya Rivera: thanks. bye.
